Explanation I states that in excluding the time during which a former suit or application was pending, the day on which that suit or application was instituted or made, and the day on which the proceedings therein ended, shall both be counted. 

 7. "Proceeding" is a term of wide amplitude. "Proceeding" is a prescribed course of action for enforcement of a legal right. The word "Proceeding" has been stated in the Black's Law Dictionary, Sixth Edition Page-1204 in the following way: 

 "An act which is done by the authority or direction of the court, agency, or tribunal, express or implied; an act necessary to be done in order to obtain a given end; a prescribed mode of action for carrying into effect a legal right. All the steps or measures adopted in the prosecution or defense of an action. Statter v. United States, C.C.A. Alaska, 66 F, 2d 819, 822. The word may be used synonymously with "action" or "suit" to describe the entire course of an action at law or suit in enquiry from the issuance of the writ or 'filing of the complaint until the entry of a final judgment or may be used to described any act done by authority of a court of law and every step required to be taken in. any cause by either party. The proceedings of a suit embrace all matters that occur in its progress judicially. 

 8. The word" Proceeding" what it connotes came up before Full Bench of Madhya Pradesh High Court in Ratanchand Darbarilal Saina and others Vs. Rajendra Kumar Khoobehand and others, AIR 1970 M.P. 1(4) F.B. wherein it has been stated that a suit, appeal or second appeal can all be described as proceeding. 

 17. Keeping in view the above stated principles and, also, paramount considerations in the matter of condonation of delay I shall now address myself to the point whether petitioner could make out a case for condonation of delay and whether the delay so caused in presenting Civil Revision Petitions before this Court can be condoned or not. 

 I. In Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case Nos. 192 of 1984 and 193 of 1984 laid under section 96 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1951 Petitioner Md. Golam Hossain is Pre-emptte and Opposite Party Abdus Sukur Bhuyan had been Pre-emptor. On the death of Pre-emptor Abdus Sukur Bhuiyan Most. Howa Bibi and others have been substituted as his legal heirs. During pendency of Civil Rules Most. Howa Bibi drew her last and her heirs had been substituted as 1 (kha)- 1(chha). 

 19. Pre-emptor opposite party by way of Counter Affidavit controverted statements made in Petition for condonation of delay. In the Counter Affidavit. Pre-emptor opposite party simply incorporated statements that Pre-emptor-Petitioner undertook untenable proceedings starting from laying Miscellaneous Appeal which was barred by limitation by 28days as well as untenable Petition under section 151 of The Code as well as Civil Revision Petitions under section 115 (I) of The Code and, also, Civil Petition for Leave to Appeals before Appellate Division. Firm assertion made by Pre-emptor opposite party is that Civil Rules stand barred by limitation as there had been a delay of 4198 days. 

 21. Ran an eye on contents contained in Petitions for condonation of delay and, also, statements contained in Counter Affidavit fled by Pre-emptor-opposite party and, also, Supplementary Affidavits laid by Pre-emptee-Petitioner. Examined documents and papers annexed in Supplementary Affidavits which have been noted in fourteenth paragraphs. 

 23. From statements made in Petition for condonation of delay as well as contents contained in Civil Revision Petitions under section 115(1) of The Code it reveals that Pre-emptee-Petitioner pursued his remedy in a wrong forum on ill advice of his learned Counsel wherein he had no hand. Considered the point that Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case was filed by Pre-emptor-opposite party after a period of long 8 years of deeds of conveyance in favour of Pre-emptee-Petitioner which is the subject matters of Pre-emption Miscellaneous. Cases under section 96 of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 24. Delaying into facts and circumstances of the case as emerged from statements made in Petitions and documents annexed as Annexures and taking into account object of doing substantial Justice to parties concerned I am of this considered view that section 14 of The Limitation Act can be very much pressed into service in support of case of Pre-emptee-Petitioner and Pre-emptee-Petitioner has made out a case which persuade me to condone the delay, though, inordinate but 'without any fault of Pre-emptee-Petitioner. Discharging Rules on technical ground of limitation would not in any way advance the interest of Justice, Fate of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case can be very much determined in Civil Revision Petitions. Is it posited here that technicality of law of limitation cannot prevent this Court from doing substantial Justice when Pre-emptee-Petitioner could make out a case for condonation of delay and, also, in getting Civil Revision Petitions heard and disposed-of on merit. It is posited here that primary function of a Court is to adjudicate disputes between the parties to advance substantial Justice. Time limit fixed for approaching the Court in different situations is not because on the expiry of such time a bad case would, transform into a good cause. If the explanation offered for condonation of delay does not smack of malafides the Court must show utmost consideration to the suitor. In Nand Kishore Vs. State of Punjab Supreme Court of India under peculiar circumstances of the case condoned the delay in approaching the Court after about 31 years. In N. Batakrishan Vs. M. Krishna Murthy Supreme Court of India held: The purpose of limitation Act was not to destroy the rights. It is founded on public policy fixing a life span for the legal remedy for general welfare.
